text: SUPERVISOR — spec refinement on RAMPREAL (queued on you), user verbatim: "ideally, a ramp is hollow underneath it. like that of fortnite. so you know you dont have to make everything suffer if u want a tall ramp, u can still have things under it so really a floor at a 45 degree angle or something like that". THE MODEL: a ramp is an INCLINED FLOOR SLAB — a thin floor tilted to span its rise (~45 nominal; the slab thickness matches the floor piece), NOT a solid wedge. Underneath is OPEN, usable space: pieces can be placed under it, characters walk under it (head clearance permitting). This refines your earlier side-band work: the catalog's "hard cover from the far side" rule is satisfied by the slab ITSELF (you cannot pass through the inclined plane) — the full-height solid side/back mass goes away; collision = the slab (walkable on top, solid through) plus its thin slab edges only. Update visual AND collision together (coherence law): hollow under-space in both. Tests: walk up the top; walk UNDER a tall ramp; place a piece under it; cannot pass through the slab itself. Slab thickness/angle are tuning data. Same SELFSHOT proof — include the under-side view. Stairs unchanged.
